claims.explanation: SB-590885 is a selective BRAF inhibitor that kills cancer lines dependent on oncogenic BRAF-driven MAPK signaling, so sensitivity is best explained by activating BRAF mutations (especially V600E) and by the absence of alternative RAS/PI3K-driven resistance. Lines with KRAS mutations or RTK/PI3K pathway alterations tend to be protected because they bypass BRAF dependence. This matches the observed enrichment of BRAF-mutant melanoma and other BRAF-mutant lineages among the most killed lines and KRAS/PIK3CA/EGFR-altered lines among the least affected.

features.basis: Oncogenic BRAF is the validated target and predicts selective MAPK inhibition (PMID 17145850, 16260133)
KRAS-driven MAPK activation bypasses BRAF dependence; KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among least affected
NRAS activates RAF/MEK/ERK downstream of BRAF and can drive BRAF-inhibitor resistance
NF1 loss activates RAS and can reduce dependence on BRAF; NF1-mutant lines appear in both extremes but mechanistically bypass BRAF
PTEN loss enhances PI3K/AKT survival signaling, a described resistance mechanism to BRAF inhibitors
PI3K pathway activation provides BRAF-independent survival; PIK3CA-mutant lines are enriched among least affected
RTK-driven MAPK/PI3K signaling can bypass BRAF inhibition; EGFR-mutant lines appear among least affected
Increased IGF-1R/PI3K signaling mediates acquired resistance to SB-590885
Higher oncogenic BRAF expression increases pathway dependence and sensitivity to BRAF inhibition
MEK mutations can activate ERK downstream of RAF and reduce sensitivity to RAF inhibition
MEK2 mutations can activate ERK downstream of RAF and reduce sensitivity to RAF inhibition
ARID1A mutations are frequent in the most killed lines, possibly reflecting chromatin-state dependency, but evidence is weaker
